title: finding(react): the designer save door `JSON.stringify`s the schema with no callable guard — a function-valued handler key is silently dropped, and reload yields a schema that lost it without an error
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:ui` execution seat as the **item-5 rider measurement** required by objectui#6124's maintainer ruling (2026-08-25): "若 objectui 存在任何「schema → JSON 序列化」出口(designer 保存等),函数值在出口必须响亮拒绝或降级为声明式形 —— `JSON.stringify` 对函数值是**静默丢弃**,正是本仓最忌的形状;服务端的 `lowerCallables` 即此步的先例." The ruling directs that a hit **files its own card and is not fixed inside that PR**. This is the hit.

Dedupe search run before filing (one targeted search; the repo-scoped `/search/issues` REST endpoint answers 403 for this seat, so this went through the MCP channel): three results, all **closed**, none on this door — #6240 (designer `fields` array-vs-map), #6309 (`serializeDesignerField` on a zero-importer bridge), #4644 (console Indexed toggle). No open card names the persistence hook.

## The door

`packages/react/src/hooks/useSchemaPersistence.ts` — the hook whose own doc comment says it "Implements schema persistence for `@object-ui/plugin-designer`".

The default adapter, used whenever a host does not inject its own:

```
packages/react/src/hooks/useSchemaPersistence.ts:58-61
    async save(id, schema) {
      const key = `${prefix}:${id}`;
      const entry = { schema, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() };
      localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(entry));
```

`JSON.stringify` drops a function-valued property **silently** — no throw, no warning, no diagnostic. `save()` resolves normally and sets `lastSavedAt`, so every observable signal reports success. The documented REST adapter in the same doc comment has the identical shape (`body: JSON.stringify(schema)`), so a host that follows the documentation inherits the behaviour rather than escaping it.

There is no callable guard anywhere on the path: no `typeof === 'function'` check, no replacer argument, no lowering step, no refusal.

## Why this is more than theoretical here

`@object-ui/types` currently declares **28 distinct keys as `z.function()`** across nine zod mirrors (`cell`, `custom`, `validate`, and 25 `on*` handlers — measured on `origin/main` `813bf8323`). Those are exactly the values a programmatic/React host puts on a schema-shaped object: measured consumption is `schema.onSelectionChange(selectedData)`, `column.cell(value, row)`, `onCardMove={schema.onCardMove}` and the like. A designer or host that round-trips such a schema through this door gets it back with those keys **gone**, and nothing anywhere says so.

The failure ordering is the bad one: the loss happens at save, the symptom appears at render or click, arbitrarily later, in a different component, with no link back to the save that caused it.

## The precedent the ruling names

objectstack's `lowerCallables` is the server-side answer to the same question: at `objectstack build`, every inline callable on a flow function is **lowered to a string ref** before the document is serialized, and the real function travels in a sibling ESM module (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow-function.zod.ts`). The value is never handed to `JSON.stringify` and quietly discarded — it is converted, deliberately, into something the serialized form can carry.

## What is NOT being asked

Not proposing an implementation. The two shapes the ruling names — **refuse loudly** at the door, or **lower** to a serializable form — are different contracts with different blast radii, and picking one is a triage call rather than a mechanical fix. Filed for triage.

Reproduce (no build needed — read the two sites):

```
sed -n '53,72p' packages/react/src/hooks/useSchemaPersistence.ts   # the adapter and its stringify
grep -rn 'z.function()' packages/types/src/zod/ | wc -l            # 60 call sites, 28 distinct keys
```

Related: #6124 (the sweep whose ruling required this measurement) - #6182 - #5250.
